paper.title_en: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
paper.abstract_en: Four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain encode a qubit over a common pure bulk ground state in a fixed symmetry sector. We determine the spatial cost of recovering it from arbitrary preselected physical spins, allowing unrestricted joint decoding. In the infinite-chain limit followed by increasing defect separation, vanishing error under linear spin budgets requires filling the central gap and at least one outer gap in density. The shorter three-defect interval attains the sharp leading cost through single-spin measurements and classical feedforward. Near-minimal successful supports approach a shortest such span in density. Below this cost, a benchmark finite-ring budget window separates entanglement-breaking connected access from entanglement-preserving single-gap perforations. For a selected two-component family, single-spin Pauli measurements and a one-way classical message yield a scale-stable Bell recovery advantage. The output channel supports positive transmission rates over independently prepared blocks, with coding performed at fixed geometry before the ordered spatial limits. Collective fusion records in discarded spins bound recovery from above, while conjugate retained records certify coherence. Finite-ring examples show that Bell-optimal one-qubit compression can reduce the full output's capacity. On two uncoupled chains with independent bulk states, a repetition embedding raises the leading cost. A matched interacting Ashkin--Teller ladder retains finite-ring geometric separation at every finite nonnegative coupling. The results distinguish useful quantum access from vanishing-error recovery and connect both to critical many-body statistics.
